text: This moon is on a slow-motion collision course with Mars. Japan just launched a heist to steal a piece of it. Step one: Mars, August 2027. Step two: drop a lookout. A 25 kilo rover. On Phobos, it weighs... 15 grams. Step three: the grab. Coring arm, nitrogen blaster. Target: at least 10 grams. Step four: one burn to leave Mars. Capsule lands in Australia, 2031. The loot? First piece of Phobos ever brought home. Next: Rocket Lab aims to launch three HawkEye 360 satellites, Wednesday. Follow Downlink Cat.
direction: You are a young, nerdy science creator in your early twenties, a little scrawny, filming a vertical video for your followers. Talk like a popular creator on TikTok or YouTube Shorts, not a narrator: conversational, a grin in your voice, genuinely hyped. Hit the hook hard, take a tiny beat before each reveal, punch the key words (collision course, heist, steal, 2027, lookout, 25, 15 grams, grab, nitrogen, 10 grams, 2031, loot, First), speed up through setup lines and slow down on the payoff. Energy: high. A little more cat: a playful purr on a few r sounds and a small 'mrr'-like rise on the question line. Still natural, never a meow.
